additionalInspected.caption:
View of the Royal Albert Hall from Prince Consort Road, showing the South Steps and the statue of Prince Consort Albert (work of Joseph Durham in 1858), to whom the hall was honored by his wife, Queen Victoria. The Royal Albert Hall is a concert hall located in South Kensington, London, England. It has a capacity of up to 5,272 seats, and since its opening by Queen Victoria in 1871, world's leading artists from several performance genres have performed there. Each year it hosts more than 350 events including The Proms concerts, that take place annually each summer since 1941.


This is a photo of listed building number 1217742.

sources.inspection: Primary designation read: elliptical Italian Renaissance red brick/buff terracotta, glazed dome; five stages, lower square-headed/upper round-headed windows, decorative pilasters/frieze; projecting cardinal porches. Photographs control current fine appearance.

Primary MOLA2020building record sections3.1.1–3.1.8 read as text: outer plan83.5m by73.2m/N–S major axis, five stages with6.1m wall separation, square and round upper window tiers, balcony, three large two-level N/E/W porches and smaller south porch. Frieze19.8m above ground/2m high; elliptical roof66.9m by56.5m raised36.6m above street,30radial trusses and13.7m central ring, ridge-and-furrow glazing. Scope excludes surveyed basement/service structures and detached chimney. PDF figures were not used or locally reproduced.

Current aerial actually inspected: oval roof with three radial glazing zones/low central oval lantern and intermediate pedimented ring, stepped oval gallery/balcony, three large projecting N/E/W porches and small south porch. Current roof broadly matches2012–14localdaylight; surrounding mansions/college/1851memorial and detached chimney are separate.
